newsitem.title: CHINA: Angang ends debut stronger than expected.
newsitem.headline: Angang ends debut stronger than expected.

text.p: Shares of Angang New Steel Co Ltd ended their first day of trade above their issue price, bucking market speculation that they may dive below their issue price due to the poor subscription response.
The H-shares of the Chinese steel producer ended at HK$1.70, up HK$0.07 or 4.29 percent from their issue price of HK$1.63.
The shares moved in a range of HK$1.63 to HK$2.00. Volume was 134.32 million shares worth HK$230.83 million.
H-shares are Chinese enterprises' shares listed in Hong Kong.
"It was well above our expectation as we expected the shares to consolidate at about their issue price," said Kelvin Tang, analysts at Impac Asset Management.
Analysts generally expected the shares to have a weak trading debut due to the cool response to the Hong Kong public offering which was undersubscribed.
China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd had bought 166 million H-shares or 7.5 percent of Angang's share capital on Wednesday, prior to their trading debut debut on Thursday.

"China Everbright taking a 7.5 percent stake in the company was seen giving investors confidence about the share price performance," said Raymond Jook, associate director of China research of SocGen Crosby Securities.
"It was seen to be the main driving force behind the rise in its (Angang) share prices," Jook said.
Angang issued 890 million H-shares at HK$1.63 per share in a global flotation. Of the total, 89 million shares offered to the public in Hong Kong were 99.7 percent subscribed.
The remaining 801 million shares which placed internationally to professional and institutional investors, were fully allotted.
Jook said China Everbright's move of taking a stake in the company might give hints of a trend that Chinese government would support H-shares companies.

"I have a feeling that the trend is establishing. It will benefit other H-shares as well and we have already upgraded some our recommendation on existing H-shares to buy or speculative buy," Jook said.

Angang is the first H-share and the first new listing on the stock exchange after Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule on July 1. The company produces steel products including cold rolled sheets, wire rods and thick plates in China.

Analysts said investors did not have a thorough understanding on the industry and a general unexciting outlook of steel industry in China had resulted in the cool response of Angang's public offering in Hong Kong.

"The (steel) industry outlook does not look very good, apart from triangular debt problems among Chinese firms, mismatch of products are seen to be the main setback on the profitability of the firms," Tang said.
"They may not produce the right products to meet the market need," he added.

Angang New Steel's deputy chairman Mu Shicheng had said in an interview on Wednesday that the poor reception of its Hong Kong public offering is due to investors' misunderstanding of its business' prospects but it expects to see steady earnings growth in the future.
Angang had said the proceeds raise from the flotation would be used to build a smelting plant in China and install pickling, rolling, cutting and packaging lines.
